name: Air France Cargo (2009 livery)
description: The passenger scheme on the two 777Fs with 'CARGO' added: all white, 'AIRFRANCE' in big navy extended capitals with the red hallmark after it, 'CARGO' in gray capitals of the same face tucked under 'FRANCE'; the navy and red fin stripes; the seahorse roundel by the nose and on the white engines.

areas.name: red stripe, tapering out toward the tip

logos.description: The Air France hallmark: a single red slash leaning forward like '/', thin at its foot and widening to the top, set just after the title's last letter (aft of it on the left side, ahead of it on the right, since it follows the text).
A small roundel with Air France's winged seahorse (hippocampe ailé) in navy line work, between the cockpit and the forward door.
The same seahorse roundel on the engine cowling.
A small ring of twelve gold stars (the European flag) on the wide navy stripe near the tip, added in 2022.

titles.style: Navy, heavy, extended geometric capitals with no space between AIR and FRANCE, upright, over the forward window line from just aft of door 1.
'CARGO' in mid-gray, the same wide capitals as 'AIRFRANCE' and about the same height, right under 'FRANCE', ending level with its E.

notes: The 2009 passenger scheme (AFR/standard) plus a gray 'CARGO' title, on F-GUOB (repainted April 2022) and F-GUOC (July 2022). Measured from F-GUOB's right side (2022-05-31) against the standard's title: 'CARGO' starts under the F of FRANCE and ends under its E, its top almost touching AIRFRANCE's baseline. No Commons photo of either from 2024-2026 yet; FlightAware logs show F-GUOC flying in June 2025. On the 777F the fin's EU stars and winglets aren't checked (no winglets: raked tips). Before 2022 both wore 'AIR FRANCE CARGO' in one line (the 2009 cargo titles). Freighters have no cabin windows. Lengths taken from A350s: on the A220 the title runs about x 0.2–0.4 with the hallmark tighter to it. The EU stars on the fin show on both A350s photographed in 2026 but may not be on the whole fleet. A dark band round the A350's engine aft of the fan cowl is probably the reverser seam and isn't drawn. A320-family winglets and the far underside weren't checked; the belly shows white from below. drawnOn B77L (2026-11-15): the freighters are 777Fs, but the 'AIRFRANCE' title's shares were taken from the A350 standard, not re-measured on a 777F (the one 777F photo, 2022, is a right-side three-quarter view); CARGO is placed against it.
history: New file. Air France's 777Fs were repainted in 2022 from 'AIR FRANCE CARGO' titles to the current AIRFRANCE titles with 'CARGO' under; A350Fs on order should arrive in it.
